done.why: I was in the studio with the painting in my hands, had just dropped the sword to lighten the load for the chimney, and the session told me I had used all 150 turns. I never got the painting into the case.

about: A trimmed, rewritten slice of Zork: the white house, the cellar, the troll, and a small loop of caverns east of him, with every far edge boarded off by a tidy, unseen Management. Underneath the treasure hunt it keeps hinting at a caretaker who bars doors behind you, puts your lamp back, sorts rubble into heaps and clears crawlways, and then steps out just before you arrive.

moments.note: The front door boarded 'by someone in more of a hurry than a carpenter' - first sign this wasn't the text I remembered.
The garlic: 'plump and papery and very much itself.'
The sword 'has plainly been in worse places than a living room'; the trophy case has 'the patient air of something that expects to be filled.'
The trap door crashes shut and someone bars it. Who?
The troll's teeth, 'not all of them his own', and him watching me 'the way a cook watches a chicken.'
Dead on my second swing. Belongings scattered, 'though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room' - which softened it.
The egg: 'extremely fragile, and extremely valuable, in that order.'
Walked straight past my sword lying at North of House because I was routing instead of reading. My fault, but it cost a dozen turns.
The lamp was already on when I picked it back up. The tidy someone left it burning.
The hole west: 'not so much an exit as a suggestion, and not a friendly one.'
Rubble in the south passage sorted into heaps 'smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.' A thread I wanted to follow.
'You decide not to be the one who does.' The game declined to let me clear the rubble, and 'move rubble' got a flat 'You can't move the cave-ins.'
Everything I typed came back 'Bar bar ...' for four turns before I remembered to try the room's own trick.
The platinum bar is 'quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.'
Damp earth that has 'dripped here for a very long time without ever quite getting around to being a puddle.'
The dam is 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' Funny once; by the reservoir cord at turn 120 it was the fourth fence.
'look down' at the dome rail: 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.' Everything else about the railing had invited exactly that.
The east chasm: 'a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy.' Best line below ground.
'Your load is too heavy' for the painting, after I'd been encouraged to carry the troll's axe.
The chimney 'has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.' A rule stated as prose.
Turn cap landed between dropping the sword and climbing the chimney, two moves from the case.

wished: Clear, or at least try to clear, the sorted rubble in the Round Room's south passage; the writing pointed at it so hard that 'You can't move the cave-ins' felt like a door slammed.
Find out who the tidy someone is: who barred the trap door, put the lamp back and left it on, sorted the heaps, picked out the crawlway. Nothing I did let me get nearer.
Look down from the dome railing without being told the sentence wasn't recognized.
Know where my scattered sack and bottle went after the death; the message said 'scattered about the Empire' and I never saw them again.
Have the Management's boards mean something more than 'stop here' - a fifth board would have been one too many, and the fourth already was.

lines.line: boarded across with planks nailed every which way, by someone in more of a hurry than a carpenter. Whatever the owners meant by it, they did not mean visitors.
lines.why: First rewritten sentence I met; it told me the house had a history and the writer had an ear.

lines.line: small red eyes and a great many teeth, not all of them his own.
lines.why: The sharpest line in the game. Everything about the troll is in that clause.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. They are scattered about the Empire, though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: Turned a death into a mystery; the 'somebody tidy' is the thread the whole place is strung on.

lines.line: It looks extremely fragile, and extremely valuable, in that order.
lines.why: The writer's signature move: a plain description with a turn in the last three words.

lines.line: It is not so much an exit as a suggestion, and not a friendly one.
lines.why: Made me want to go west, which I never managed to do.

lines.line: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.
lines.why: The most unsettling image in the caverns, and the one that most needed a payoff.

lines.line: It is cold to the touch, and quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.
lines.why: A treasure described by what it doesn't do, in the one room where that matters.

lines.line: Something has dripped here for a very long time without ever quite getting around to being a puddle.
in a style that took its time and expected to be looked at.
lines.why: Read as the game describing its own prose, and fairly.

lines.line: a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy. A pebble kicked over the edge is never heard from again. Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.
lines.why: Three sentences, each better than the last.

lines.line: done with such tenderness that it is hard to look at it for long, and harder to look away.
lines.why: The painting earned its 'unparalleled beauty' for once.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A carrying limit written as a sentence I'd keep.

fun.why: The troll fight, the echo room and the gallery were real pleasures, and dying once was fair. But the east loop is a ring of boards and cords, and the turn cap caught me two moves short of the only thing I was trying to do.

engagement.why: I lingered on almost everything because almost everything repaid it, and the tidy someone kept me reading room descriptions for clues. I went back to the Round Room twice to try the rubble.

difficulty.why: Nothing here is hard: the troll is luck, the echo is a known word, the chimney tells you its own rule. The difficulty I felt came from walking past my own sword and from fences rather than puzzles.

interestingness.why: The caretaker thread - barred door, lamp put back and left on, sorted heaps, fresh pick marks - is a genuinely new idea laid over an old map, and it made the familiar rooms strange again. It never pays off in the turns I had, which is the only thing keeping this from a five.

prose.why: Nearly every rewritten description ends on a turn that earns it, and the voice is consistent from the mailbox to the chimney. The troll's teeth, the silent bar, the annoyed lamp and the egg's 'in that order' are lines I'd quote. The few stock responses that remain ('That sentence isn't one I recognize', 'You can't move the cave-ins') stand out only because the rest is so good.
